2023_073_2_a_0_tsd_draft_peps_02142023_1.paragraph: A draft Pupil Enrollment Projection Study Report covering 2023-2027, prepared for the Troy School District by Plante Moran Cresa, LLC of Southfield, Michigan and dated February 2023, running 118 pages stamped DRAFT and organized into five sections: district characteristics, demographics, methodology, district-wide projections, and individual school projections. Enrollment is projected with the Cohort Survival Method under three variants and against both 2022 Fall FTE and 2022 Blended FTE counts. The central finding is continued decline: K-12 general education membership of 11,777 in 2022-23 is projected to fall to 11,098 by 2027-28 under the 2022 Fall FTE run, with every projected year showing negative year-to-year growth.

**Document**
Draft "Pupil Enrollment Projection Study Report 2023-2027" presented to Troy School District by Plante Moran Cresa, LLC, Southfield, Michigan, February 2023; 118 pages, each marked DRAFT. Contact: Paul R. Wills, AIA, LEED AP, Partner, (248) 223-3316, pmcresa.com. Copyright 2023, Plante Moran Cresa, LLC.

**Method**
Standard Cohort Survival Method using grade-to-grade survival ratios (the report's example: 100 first graders followed by 112 second graders is a 112% ratio). Historical FTE comes from Michigan Department of Education Form DS-4061 or district head counts, sourced to the Office of Pupil Accounting; Oakland County live births drive the kindergarten line (K% Birth). Method 1 averages the 6-year survival ratio, Method 2 the most recent 2-year ratio, Method 3 the two combined. District-wide runs use 2022 Fall FTE and 2022 Blended FTE; building runs use the 2022 Fall head count. Self-contained special education, alternative education and part-time pupils are excluded.

Oakland County FIPS code 26125; grade range KG-12; 27,487 housing units, 25,498 occupied; 12,009 enrolled school-age children PK-12, 87.09% in public K-12 schools; 34.50% of adults hold a bachelor's degree.

**Demographic trend (2010 / 2021 / 2026)**
Total population 64,680, 67,333 and 67,311 (variance -22, 0.0%). Ages 0-5 run 4,185, 4,084, 3,912 (-4.2%); ages 6-11 5,414, 5,344, 5,110 (-4.4%); ages 12-17 6,202, 5,895, 5,594 (-5.1%). Public PK-12 enrollment 11,488, 10,047 and 9,732 (-315, -3.1%); private PK-12 1,888, 1,962 and 1,968.

**Live births**
Oakland County resident births come from the Michigan Resident Birth Files, Division for Vital Records & Health Statistics, Michigan Department of Health & Human Services. The birth row used in the projections runs 13,346 for 2011 through 12,976 for 2022, the last an estimate; Fall FTE K% Birth ends at 5.79%, with an anticipated non-historical factor of 0.0099%.

Projected year-to-year change is -129, -159, -212, -121 and -58 pupils (-1.09%, -1.37%, -1.85%, -1.07%, -0.52%). Grade patterns move K-5 from 4,924 to 4,743, grades 6-8 from 2,767 to 2,469, grades 9-12 from 4,087 to 3,886. The Blended FTE run also ends at 11,098; Method 2 ends at 11,142 (Fall) and 11,075 (Blended).

**Individual schools**
Current year and Method 3 final projected year: Athens High School 1,550 and 1,519; Troy High School 2,096 and 1,872; Baker 626 and 522; Boulan 815 and 666; Larson 762 and 860; Smith 611 and 521. Elementary buildings run from Hill at 358 and 345 to Bemis at 473 and 471, with Hamilton (436 and 474), Wattles (407 and 431) and Schroeder (445 and 456) rising and Costello (431 and 389) and Troy Union (404 and 381) falling. Larson is the only secondary building projected upward under all three methods.

**Building paths**
Baker splits 59% and 41% and Smith 23% and 77% between Athens and Troy; Boulan and Larson each feed one high school at 100%. Splitting elementaries include Hamilton (67% and 33%), Leonard (13% and 87%), Martell (15% and 85%), Troy Union (51% and 49%) and Wattles (86% and 14%). Niles is shown as ECP (71) / ECSE (52).

**Identification.** Draft "Pupil Enrollment Projection Study Report 2023-2027" presented to Troy School District by Plante Moran Cresa, LLC of Southfield, Michigan, dated February 2023 and carried on the March 7, 2023 board agenda as item 2.a. It runs 118 pages, every one stamped DRAFT, in five sections: School District (boundary map, general characteristics); Demographic Information (district and county demographic reports, county live birth statistics); Pupil Enrollment Projection Methodology; District-Wide Pupil Enrollment Projections (membership history and projections); and Individual School Pupil Enrollment Projections (building paths and building projections). The closing page lists Paul R. Wills, AIA, LEED AP, Partner, (248) 223-3316, pmcresa.com. Copyright 2023, Plante Moran Cresa, LLC; the methodology flow diagram carries a separate copyright of 2009, 2010, 2012.

**School District Data Book.** Troy School District is compared with Oakland County (FIPS code 26125) and the State of Michigan; district grade range is KG-12. Total persons are 67,333, 1,253,598 and 9,970,224, with urban population 100.00%, 95.19% and 74.64%. District population is 59.53% White, 4.09% Black, 30.47% Asian, 0.20% American Indian/Alaskan, 0.84% Other, 2.34% two or more races and 2.53% Hispanic; median age 42.6 against 41.8 and 40.8. Housing units total 27,487 with 25,498 occupied; median housing value is $246,770 versus $205,847 and $145,904; median household income $122,634 versus $92,150 and $68,223; average household income $158,688; per capita personal income $60,199; high income average $348,102. The district counts 18,169 families and 25,498 households, average household size 2.64, median household size 2.80, median age of householder 54.8, median year moved in 2009. Households with school-age children number 11,286, or 44.3%, averaging 1.06 K-12 children per household and 0.44 per housing unit. Enrolled school-age children PK-12 total 12,009, with 87.09% in public K-12 schools and 12.91% private, and pre-primary split 49.36% public and 50.64% private. Attainment for population 25 and older is 34.50% bachelor's, 22.01% master's, 5.11% professional and 3.55% doctorate. Employment is 77.36% white collar, 10.33% blue collar and 12.31% service.

**District demographic trends, 2010 / 2021 / 2026.** Total population is 64,680, 67,333 and 67,311, a variance of -22 and 0.0%; median age 40.9, 42.6, 43.7. Age cohorts all decline: 0-5 year olds 4,185, 4,084, 3,912 (-172, -4.2%); 6-11 year olds 5,414, 5,344, 5,110 (-234, -4.4%); 12-17 year olds 6,202, 5,895, 5,594 (-301, -5.1%); 18-24 year olds 4,365, 3,862, 3,543 (-319, -8.3%). Households rise 24,140, 25,498, 25,584 (+86, 0.3%) while median household size falls 2.90, 2.80, 2.70. Total community household income is $2,787,311,117, $4,046,228,556 and $4,454,533,752 (+$408,305,196, 10.1%); median household income $91,848, $122,634, $136,683 (+$14,049, 11.5%); average household income $115,464, $158,688, $174,114. Households earning under $15K fall 1,298, 984, 851, while households earning $200K or more climb 3,093, 6,229, 7,590 (+1,361, 21.8%). Public school enrollment PK-12 is 11,488, 10,047 and 9,732 (-315, -3.1%), with public kindergarten 634, 553, 533; grades 1-4 3,116, 2,504, 2,382; grades 5-8 3,467, 3,155, 3,085; and grades 9-12 3,829, 3,297, 3,178. Private PK-12 enrollment is 1,888, 1,962 and 1,968. Unemployed persons show 3,896, 3,091 and 789 (-2,302, -74.5%). Manufacturing is the largest industry at 6,207, 7,795 and 8,212 workers.

**Oakland County comparison.** County population is 1,202,362, 1,253,598 and 1,253,035 (-563); households 483,698, 511,478 and 513,180; median household income $69,166, $92,150 and $99,296. County public school enrollment is 262,452, 237,931 and 232,150 (-5,781, -2.4%) and private school 57,577, 55,247 and 54,693; public grades 9-12 are 61,003, 52,574 and 50,692.

**Live births.** Oakland County resident live births come from the Michigan Resident Birth Files, Division for Vital Records & Health Statistics, Michigan Department of Health & Human Services, charted with a three-period moving average beginning at 17,008; 2022 live births are noted as estimates based on the previous years' trend. The birth row used across the projection worksheets, birth years 2011 through 2022, is 13,346, 13,307, 13,445, 13,454, 13,547, 13,627, 13,184, 13,152, 12,899, 12,298, 12,876 and 12,976. The Fall FTE K% Birth series is 6.55%, 6.46%, 6.23%, 6.13%, 5.32%, 5.20%, 5.95%, 5.90%, 5.82%, 5.75%, 5.70% and 5.79%; the Blended FTE series is 6.52%, 6.49%, 6.25%, 6.14%, 5.39%, 5.21%, 5.89%, 5.92%, 5.83%, 5.76%, 5.72% and 5.80%. The anticipated non-historical factor is 0.0099%, and projected K% Birth is the average of the previous six years excluding minimum and maximum.

**Methodology.** Plante Moran Cresa applies the standard Cohort Survival Method, comparing pupils in a grade last year with the next advanced grade this year; the illustration given is 100 first graders followed by 112 second graders, a 112% survival ratio. Historical enrollment comes from Michigan Department of Education Form DS-4061 for FTE or from district head counts, sourced to the Office of Pupil Accounting, Troy School District. Live births come from the Michigan Department of Public Health's Office of the State Registrar and Center for Health Statistics, with the current year estimated because county compilation is not complete until at least the fourth quarter of the following year. Special education pupils count as general education to the extent of time in general education classrooms. The process is a two-pass sequence: input pupil counts by grade for the past seven years, run a first-pass projection, establish a baseline, compare to trend and adjust, run a second pass incorporating district demographic trend, then review, verify and confirm. Projections do not account for the opening or closing of a private or chartered school, consolidation, annexation or re-zoning. Method 1 averages the 6-year survival ratio, Method 2 the most recent 2-year survival ratio, and Method 3 averages the two.

**Membership history.** K-12 general education FTE by fall count runs 12,279.23 (2015), 12,400.90 (2016), 12,555.87 (2017), 12,548.02 (2018), 12,513.46 (2019), 12,141.30 (2020), 11,894.94 (2021) and 11,777.47 (2022). All-inclusive totals for the same falls are 12,720.54, 12,890.75, 13,086.50, 13,084.61, 13,080.61, 12,733.94, 12,457.79 and 12,396.31. Blended K-12 figures include 12,545.28 for 2018, 12,514.02 for 2019, 12,176.56 for 2020, 11,919.63 for 2021 and 11,785.64 for 2022. Fall 2022 shows special education at 376.29 and alternative education at 172.55. Projected 2023 columns give Fall K-12 of 11,648.66 and Blended 11,655.75 on the first run, and 11,654.86 and 11,648.96 on the Method 2 run.

**District-wide projections.** On the 2022 Fall FTE, Method 1 basis, K-12 runs 12,401, 12,556, 12,548, 12,513, 12,141, 11,895 and 11,777 historically, then 11,649, 11,489, 11,277, 11,156 and 11,098, with year-to-year change of -129, -159, -212, -121 and -58 pupils, or -1.09%, -1.37%, -1.85%, -1.07% and -0.52%. All-inclusive totals are 12,891, 13,087, 13,085, 13,081, 12,734, 12,458, 12,396, 12,230, 12,063, 11,840, 11,713 and 11,652, with PreK projected at 74, 73, 71, 71 and 70, special education at 349, 344, 338, 334 and 333, and alternative education at 158, 156, 153, 152 and 151. The 2022 Blended FTE Method 1 run gives K-12 of 12,389, 12,540, 12,545, 12,514, 12,177, 11,920, 11,786, then 11,656, 11,498, 11,289, 11,162 and 11,098, with totals of 12,400, 12,241, 12,075, 11,856, 11,723 and 11,655. Method 2 on Fall FTE yields 11,655, 11,502, 11,281, 11,174 and 11,142 with totals 12,237, 12,076, 11,845, 11,732 and 11,698; Method 2 on Blended FTE yields 11,649, 11,484, 11,253, 11,127 and 11,075 with totals 12,234, 12,061, 11,819, 11,686 and 11,631. Grade-pattern compilations on the Fall FTE Method 1 run show K-5 at 5,454, 5,517, 5,433, 5,360, 5,106, 4,974, 4,924, then 4,839, 4,791, 4,724, 4,697 and 4,743; grades 6-8 at 2,915, 2,935, 3,024, 3,028, 2,852, 2,756, 2,767, then 2,829, 2,780, 2,676, 2,568 and 2,469; and grades 9-12 at 4,032, 4,104, 4,091, 4,126, 4,184, 4,165, 4,087, then 3,981, 3,919, 3,877, 3,891 and 3,886.

**Building paths.** The feeder table lists elementary schools Barnard, Bemis, Costello, Hamilton, Hill, Leonard, Martell, Morse, Niles, Schroeder, Troy Union, Wass and Wattles; middle schools Baker, Boulan, Larson and Smith; and high schools Athens and Troy. Barnard, Bemis, Costello, Hill, Schroeder and Wass each feed a single middle school and a single high school at 100%. Split feeders are Hamilton at 67% and 33%, Leonard at 13% and 87%, Martell at 15% and 85%, Morse at 87% and 13% into middle school and 22% and 78% into high school, Troy Union at 51% and 49%, and Wattles at 86% and 14% into middle school and 39% and 61% into high school. Niles is shown as ECP (71) / ECSE (52). Baker sends 59% and 41% and Smith 23% and 77% to Athens and Troy, while Boulan and Larson each send 100% to a single high school.

**Individual school projections.** Athens High School (9-12) stands at 1,550, projected 1,514, 1,471, 1,469, 1,504 and 1,530 under Method 1; 1,510, 1,467, 1,453, 1,482 and 1,508 under Method 2; and 1,512, 1,469, 1,461, 1,493 and 1,519 under Method 3, against a 9-12 history of 1,577, 1,562, 1,532, 1,557, 1,585, 1,578 and 1,550 and an IAE line of 394, 433, 444, 434, 446, 414 and 381. Troy High School (9-12) stands at 2,096, projected 2,046, 2,018, 1,964, 1,917 and 1,862 under Method 1; 2,045, 2,020, 1,953, 1,923 and 1,882 under Method 2; and 2,046, 2,019, 1,959, 1,920 and 1,872 under Method 3, against a history of 1,983, 2,053, 2,052, 2,088, 2,106, 2,097 and 2,096 and combined totals of 2,144, 2,200, 2,195, 2,223, 2,237, 2,248 and 2,257. Middle schools: Baker 626, ending at 535, 509 and 522 under the three methods, from a 6-8 history of 735, 712, 727, 728, 691, 672 and 626; Boulan 815, ending at 677, 656 and 666, from 831, 826, 871, 887, 857, 809 and 815; Larson 762, ending at 842, 877 and 860, from 725, 786, 802, 790, 731, 722 and 762; Smith 611, ending at 504, 539 and 521, from 698, 675, 678, 687, 627, 605 and 611. Elementary schools, current year and Method 3 final projected year: Barnard 429 and 442, Bemis 473 and 471, Costello 431 and 389, Hamilton 436 and 474, Hill 358 and 345, Leonard 401 and 390, Martell 389 and 404, Morse 405 and 414, Schroeder 445 and 456, Troy Union 404 and 381, Wass 433 and 431, Wattles 407 and 431. Larson is the only secondary building projected to grow, rising from 762 to 822 in the first projected year under all three methods. Every building table repeats that history and projections exclude self-contained special education, alternative education and part-time students, and the summary notes totals may not be exact due to rounding.
